- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: lines 137-141 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Module-level control-flow AST nodes are treated as indeterminate, causing common Python files to lose complete causal scope.
  WHY: Waiver revalidation then rejects those findings as indeterminate, causing pre-existing defects to be re-reported on every audit cycle.
- scripts/model_provider_proxy.py: lines 113-119, 256-292 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A single upstream response with missing or unparsable usage cost permanently marks accounting as failed.
  WHY: Subsequent legitimate requests are rejected with 429, halting editor and reviewer runs.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 1469-1485 (within `normalize_finding`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Failed or unmatched git blame falls back to the audited head SHA as provenance even when that commit did not introduce the finding.
  WHY: Waiver keys can bind to incorrect provenance and become incorrectly retained or re-issued after history changes.
- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh: lines 68-79,315-417 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup trap waits indefinitely for the proxy after sending SIGTERM and has no bounded escalation.
  WHY: A stuck proxy can block the sandbox wrapper and leave the GitHub Actions job hanging.
- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh: lines 193-211 (safe_git_config construction) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `remote.<name>.pushurl` and `[url] "insteadOf"` rewrites remain available despite remote URL sanitization.
  WHY: Sandboxed git operations can still resolve to attacker-controlled destinations and exfiltrate repository contents.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 4728-4731 (and matching jq in security_audit.sh) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Unknown or missing legacy `causal_scope_status` values are silently rewritten to `indeterminate`.
  WHY: Older waivers then fail strict revalidation and reappear as blocking findings without an operator-visible diagnostic.
- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh: lines 196-211 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Git configuration sanitization leaves `insteadOf`, proxy, template-directory, and related trust-boundary settings available.
  WHY: A model can route git traffic through attacker-controlled infrastructure or influence filesystem behavior during later git operations.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: lines 137-141 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_symbols_for_source` sets `module_indeterminate = True` for any module-level AST node that is not in the explicit allowlist `(ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom, ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign, ast.AugAssign, ast.Expr, ast.Pass)`.
  WHY: Any Python finding's waiver will fail closed on the very first re-audit because the validator cannot compute a complete causal scope for the cited file.
- scripts/model_provider_proxy.py: lines 113-119, 256-292 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `ProxyAccounting.settle()` sets `self.accounting_failed = True` whenever `actual_cost is None`.
  WHY: A single upstream response that lacks the `cost` key permanently causes subsequent `reserve()`/`add_reservation()` calls to reject with 429.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 1469-1485 (within `normalize_finding`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `git blame` returns non-zero or no commit matches the blame regex, the function falls back to using `audit_scope_head_sha` as `provenance_commit`.
  WHY: The key can be bound to a commit that did not actually introduce the line, causing legitimate waivers to be incorrectly retained or re-issued.
- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh: lines 68-79,315-417 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The cleanup trap kills `proxy_pid` and then calls `wait "${proxy_pid}"` with no timeout.
  WHY: If the proxy does not exit promptly, the sandbox wrapper blocks indefinitely and the GitHub Actions job never finishes.
- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh: lines 193-211 (safe_git_config construction) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `safe_git_config` rewrites `remote.<name>.url` but does not touch `remote.<name>.pushurl` or `[url] "insteadOf"` rewrite rules.
  WHY: A model can configure git to push commits to an attacker-controlled host and exfiltrate staged changes.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 4728-4731 (and matching jq in security_audit.sh) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The poller rewrites any `causal_scope_status` other than `"complete"` or `"indeterminate"` to `"indeterminate"`.
  WHY: Legacy keyless waivers silently stop suppressing re-reports because strict revalidation requires `"complete"`.
- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh: lines 196-211 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The sandbox leaves `[url] insteadOf`, `http.*`, `core.gitProxy`, `remote.<name>.proxy`, `init.templateDir`, and related settings in scope.
  WHY: A model process can route git traffic through attacker-controlled infrastructure or gain filesystem trust through git template configuration.
- scripts/model_provider_proxy.py: _begin_accounted_request / _proxy_accounted_request accounting path
  PROBLEM: A single missing-cost response permanently fails accounting; subsequent legitimate responses are blocked.
  WHY: Track consecutive missing-cost responses or continue accepting requests up to the spend limit while exposing a warning.
- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh: safe_git_config construction (lines 193-211)
  PROBLEM: Git proxy, templateDir, and insteadOf rewriting is incomplete.
  WHY: Also strip `[url] "insteadOf"` rules, `remote.<name>.pushurl`, `http.*.sslCAInfo`, `http.*.proxy`, `core.gitProxy`, `init.templateDir`, and `remote.<name>.proxy`.
- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: module-level AST check (lines 137-141)
  PROBLEM: Every non-trivial module body is marked indeterminate, blocking common `if __name__ == "__main__":` idioms.
  WHY: Allow module-level control-flow wrappers when their bodies contain no indeterminate calls.

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
